A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Covariance Density Neural Networks. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original financial forecasting and EEG classification results in Tables 1–2, plus original ablations and synthetic experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original financial forecasting and EEG classification results, retains the appendix experiments, and adds financial β and runtime scalability analyses.

M1.justification: The density transform and multiscale CDNN formulation remain. v2 introduces a hybrid applying attention after multiscale covariance-density filtering. Appendix A.2 also extends the stated omission of the unfiltered k=0 term from EEG datasets to all datasets.

E1.justification: Both retain Exchange Rate, S&P 500, US Stock, binary and four-class BCI-2A, PhysioNet, and the same synthetic scenarios. The new financial ablation uses the existing US Stock task; channel-count scaling changes experimental configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Financial Table 1 adds GCN and the CDNN–attention Hybrid alongside the retained VNN, CDNN, GIN, and GAT comparisons. The EEG and synthetic regression comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Financial Table 3 changes dropout from 0.5 to 0.2 and β initialization from four zeros to [-0.01, 0.01, 0, 0]. New experiments introduce fixed-β sweeps and cached-versus-recomputed runtime controls across channel counts. Figure 1 changes the labeled validation quantity from density-eigenvalue differences to filter-response differences. Existing splits, horizons, and EEG cross-validation designs remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the diagnostics with US Stock horizon-3 β sensitivity and learned-β trajectories, plus a runtime scalability and caching study (Appendices A.4–A.5, Figures 6–7). Figures 1–2 also revise the Lipschitz-validation and entropy demonstrations. Earlier EEG ablations, reconstruction studies, and synthetic noise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Financial results retain mean and standard deviation over three seeds; EEG results retain variation across subjects or folds. The added runtime curves continue mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over seeds. No new statistical estimation method or increased run count for retained experiments is stated.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces financial scores and substantially changes rankings. For Exchange horizon 1, v1 reports GAT 0.0876 and CDNN 0.3164; v2 reports GAT 0.1819, CDNN 0.1102, and Hybrid 0.1057. These accompany revised settings and are not same-setting gains. Figures 1–2 change numerical content, and new ablation/runtime results appear. Main EEG scores are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds an explicit computational-complexity account: O(m³) preprocessing and O(Km²) per order-K filter under caching. The existing definitions, stability and equivariance theorems, entropy results, reconstruction objective, and appendix proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the covariance-density GSO, multiscale spectral discrimination, β-controlled stability, covariance entropy, improved forecasting over VNNs, and efficient subject-independent EEG classification. The revised abstract and introduction emphasize these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies quasi-Hamiltonian as a spectral analogy and adds interpretations concerning financial risk awareness and computational scalability. It also newly claims trace normalization induces scale invariance, which conflicts with the retained scale-sensitive CVNE analysis. The stated limitations concerning second-order statistics and static covariance remain.

D1.justification: New Section 4.1 explains covariance construction, while Section 4.4 and Appendix A.5 disclose eigendecomposition, caching, and memory considerations. Hyperparameter documentation is revised. Hardware and data-access information remain substantially unchanged, and Table 3 does not provide corresponding configuration rows for the newly evaluated GCN and Hybrid.

R1.justification: v2 removes several references, including Sihag et al. on VNN transferability and Levie et al. on spectral transferability. Its introduction more explicitly positions CDNN against VNN spectral-control and noise limitations. Most foundational positioning remains; the author–year citation conversion is primarily stylistic.

P1.justification: The introduction is expanded, and Section 2 gains a tutorial overview connecting GSP, GNNs, covariance, and density matrices. New covariance-construction and computational-cost subsections improve organization. Most methodological exposition, conclusions, and appendix proof narratives remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises visual presentation: Figures 1–3 are redrawn, Figures 6–7 are added, Table 1 gains comparator rows, and the main tables replace text-wrapped arrangements with standalone blocks. Retained appendix figures are enlarged and redistributed. Figure 3 removes the earlier numerical color scales for individual panels.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful financial β diagnostics, scalability measurements, and clearer background, addressing gaps in v1. However, its claim that all experiments cache the exponential once conflicts with the learned β trajectories in Figure 6, and its new scale-invariance explanation conflicts with the retained scale-sensitive entropy analysis. These unresolved inconsistencies, alongside unexplained numerical revisions in Figures 1–2, prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
